project-charter.title: 1. Engineering Problem Charter: Heavy Conveyor Spur Drive

cards.title: Industrial Situation & Transmission Brief
cards.body: A heavy-duty bulk material conveyor system in an industrial processing plant requires an enclosed single-stage spur gear reduction unit. The driving electric motor delivers rated power P = 11.0 kW at N1 = 960 rpm. The driven conveyor head pulley shaft must operate at N2 = 320 rpm (transmission ratio i = 3.00). An initial trial configuration has been proposed with a 20-tooth pinion and a 60-tooth gear, using standard module m = 4.0 mm, face width b = 40.0 mm, and 20° full-depth involute teeth. The transmission must achieve a minimum operational factor of safety [FOS] >= 1.50 under continuous duty.

cards.title: Design Specifications & Material Properties
cards.body:
The engineering department has specified the following preliminary materials and service conditions:
• Pinion Material: 40Ni2Cr1Mo28 alloy steel (Sut1 = 800 MPa, Surface Hardness = 350 BHN)
• Gear Material: 55C8 plain carbon steel (Sut2 = 600 MPa, Surface Hardness = 250 BHN)
• Application Service Factor: Ka = 1.50 (heavy conveyor shock duty)
• Load Distribution Factor: Km = 1.25
• Tooth Profile: Standard 20° full-depth involute (Y = 0.484 - 2.87/z)
• Target Safety Factor: [FOS] = 1.50

cards.title: Engineering Responsibility & Failure Consequences
cards.body: Conveyor drives in heavy industry operate under severe cyclic torque spikes. Catastrophic tooth breakage stops the entire continuous processing line, causing major economic loss. Meanwhile, surface contact fatigue (wear/pitting) leads to severe noise, vibration, and tooth spalling. The design engineer must evaluate both tooth root beam strength (Lewis equation) and surface wear durability (Buckingham equation) to ensure a safe, robust transmission.

project-charter.acceptanceText: I have reviewed the Heavy Conveyor Spur Gearbox Design Brief and understand that I must evaluate beam strength, wear durability, dynamic loading, and perform redesign optimizations to ensure operational safety under PCC353-MEC (CO1).

material-and-failure.title: 5. Material Selection & Gear-Tooth Failure Evaluation
material-and-failure.prompt: Evaluate permissible bending stresses and identify the primary failure modes governing spur gear durability.
material-and-failure.description: Calculate permissible bending stresses (sigma_b = Sut / 3) for both materials and analyze failure mechanisms.
given: Pinion Material: 40Ni2Cr1Mo28 alloy steel (Sut1 = 800 MPa, 350 BHN)
Gear Material: 55C8 plain carbon steel (Sut2 = 600 MPa, 250 BHN)
Design Basis: Factor of Safety on Ultimate Tensile Strength = 3.0

mcq.question: Which pair of failure mechanisms represents the two primary design criteria evaluated in spur gear transmission rating?

options.label: Beam bending fatigue failure at tooth root and contact fatigue / surface pitting failure on tooth flank
Centrifugal rim bursting and shear failure of hub mounting bolts
Excessive torsional deflection of teeth and plastic yielding at the tip
High temperature creep deformation and oxidative tooth erosion

lewis-beam-strength.title: 6. Lewis Form Factors & Beam Strength Calculation
lewis-beam-strength.figure: Lewis Tooth Form Factor & Beam Strength Evaluation
lewis-beam-strength.description: Calculate Lewis form factors, determine the weaker element governing bending strength, and compute Lewis beam strength (Sb) and bending safety factor (FOSb).
given: 20° Full-Depth Involute Lewis Formula: Y = 0.484 - 2.87 / z
Pinion Teeth: z1 = 20, Gear Teeth: z2 = 60
Module: m = 4.0 mm, Face Width: b = 40.0 mm
Permissible Stresses: sigma_b1 = 266.67 MPa, sigma_b2 = 200.00 MPa
Target Factor of Safety: [FOS] = 1.50

formulas.name: Lewis Beam Strength (Sb)
formulas.formula: Sb = m * b * sigma_b * Y [N] (evaluated for the weaker element)

failure-diagnosis.title: 9. Initial Failure Diagnosis & Root Cause Assessment
failure-diagnosis.prompt: Evaluate the bending and wear safety factors to identify the governing failure mode and the required design remedy.
failure-diagnosis.description: Synthesize the mechanical performance of the initial trial gear set and diagnose the governing failure mode.
given: Bending Factor of Safety: FOSb = 2.00 (Target [FOS] = 1.50 -> SAFE)
Wear Factor of Safety: FOSw = 0.689 (Target [FOS] = 1.50 -> UNSAFE)
Governing Defect: Severe contact stress leading to surface pitting / spalling

mcq.question: Based on the calculated factors of safety (FOSb = 2.00 vs FOSw = 0.689 against target [FOS] = 1.50), what is the governing failure mode and required engineering action?

options.label: Governing mode is Surface Wear / Pitting Fatigue (FOSw = 0.689 < 1.50, UNSAFE); beam bending strength is adequate (FOSb = 2.00 >= 1.50). Parametric redesign must enhance contact durability.
Governing mode is Tooth Bending Fracture at the root; tooth wear durability is well within safe operating limits.
Both bending and wear durability are fully compliant; no parametric redesign is necessary.
Both bending and wear fail catastrophically; the gear transmission ratio must be completely inverted.

parametric-redesign.title: 10. Parametric Redesign Computations (Options A, B, C)
parametric-redesign.description: Calculate wear durability for three engineering redesign proposals to determine which options achieve the target FOS >= 1.50.
given: Initial Condition: Sw = 4800 N, Peff = 6965.67 N -> FOSw = 0.689 (Unsafe)
Option A: Increase face width to b = 60 mm (original m = 4 mm, 250 BHN)
Option B: Increase gear tooth surface hardness to 400 BHN (original m = 4 mm, b = 40 mm)
Option C: Increase module to m = 5 mm, face width b = 60 mm (gear hardness = 250 BHN)

formulas.name: Option B Load-Stress Factor & Wear Strength
Option C Pitch Diameter, Dynamic Load & Wear Strength

fields.label: Option C Pinion Pitch Diameter (m = 5 mm)
